title: Lady Astor and Churchill: The Poisoned Coffee
summary: 'Winston, if you were my husband, I'd poison your coffee!' snapped Lady Astor. 'Madam, if you were my wife, I'd drink it!' replied Churchill.
keywords: Lady Astor and Churchill: The Poisoned Coffee
full_text:
In the British House of Commons, few rivalries were as fiercely entertaining as that between Winston Churchill and Lady Nancy Astor, the first woman to take a seat in the British Parliament.

During an aristocratic country house weekend, Lady Astor found herself thoroughly enraged by Churchill's political views.

Unable to restrain her exasperation, she glared across the breakfast room and snapped:
**"Winston! If you were my husband, I'd poison your coffee!"**

The gathered guests froze in shock at the venomous outburst.

Churchill slowly lowered his morning paper, peered over his spectacles, and answered with absolute equanimity:
**"Madam! If you were my wife, I'd drink it!"**

The room erupted in laughter. Churchill turned an aggressive insult into an instant triumph of wit, proving that good humor is the ultimate retort to hostility.
moral: Responding to spite with spontaneous wit defuses aggression and turns provocation into comedy.
